quote: Twenty two Flock cameras currently line the roads in Pawtucket, recording, detecting and storing the license plate and vehicle information of passing cars.
notes: Operating; installed count. Earlier coverage: 17 cameras in 2021 regional trial, about 20 in 2023 paid deployment; Uprise RI (Aug 2026) says portal lists 22.

quote: Woonsocket's portal, marked July 25, displayed 15 cameras, 113 searches and a long roster of organizations granted access
notes: Operating; per transparency portal as reported by Uprise RI (Sept 15, 2026). Valley Breeze (Jan 2025) also reported the city's 15 Flock Safety cameras; council voted 5-1 in Sept 2026 to keep them.

quote: renewed Warwick’s expiring 2-year Flock camera deal to operate 11 license plate cameras in the city for the Warwick Police Department.
notes: Operating; council renewed contract July 2025. Original 2023 purchase was for 10 cameras.

quote: the last of the eight to be erected went up around Dec. 17
notes: Operating; all eight cameras live as of January 2026 article (headline: Eight criminal-catching cameras now live in North Providence).

quote: Cumberland's 12 Flock cameras are part of a network of automated license-plate readers now operating in dozens of Rhode Island communities
notes: Operating; count matches town transparency portal as described in article. Another source about 50 days earlier reportedly said 10.

quote: Narragansett now has three Flock cameras.
notes: Council voted Aug 3, 2026 to end contract; cameras cancelled and to be removed. Four originally installed, one stolen.

quote: terminate its contract with the company and remove its six cameras from town roads.
notes: Council voted 3-2 on Aug 17/18, 2026 to cancel contract; six cameras removed.

quote: The town put up seven cameras in total.
notes: Council voted unanimously July 27, 2026 to cancel contract and remove cameras. Other outlets describe six or a half-dozen cameras.

quote: Harrisburg Police's Lt. Kyle Gautsch said there are roughly 50 license plate readers installed at intersections across the city.
notes: Approximate count ("roughly 50"); installed at intersections, grant-funded (PCCD); operating as of Nov 2025. Vendor not stated.

quote: Abington has one permanent Flock camera up in the township and a few cameras the department keeps at the station and deploys as needed, Deputy Chief Ed Quinn said.
notes: Count is the single permanent (fixed) Flock camera; excludes portable units deployed as needed. Flock contracts ending; on Aug 27, 2026 commissioners voted to drop the Flock system (Fox 29 described it as three cameras, likely incl. portable) and approved 2 Axon cameras instead.

quote: He says the department operates 9 Flock cameras around the township, costing more than $46,000 a year.
notes: Operating; Salem Township, Luzerne County (near Berwick). WNEP story syndicated on Yahoo; system in place since 2023.

quote: Hazleton has 60 flock cameras located throughout the city.
notes: Operating; WBRE/28-22 News story syndicated on Yahoo. Caveat: article says the system records video and sound, so the 60 may include Flock video cameras, not only license plate readers; city was adding more cameras under a $4M 10-year upgrade.

quote: The NYPD already has some 500 license plate readers of its own that combine with feeds from surveillance cameras, 911 calls, gunshot and radiation detectors, criminal database information, and other sources as part of the department's Domain Awareness System .
notes: Approximate ("some 500"); dated 2016 figure, no newer official or news-quoted NYPD count found. Fixed vs vehicle-mounted split not stated (NYPD uses both fixed and mobile LPRs per its 2026 Impact and Use Policy). Brennan Center (2019) also cites "nearly 500". Operating; no Flock contract in NYC.

quote: Police told WFMZ this week that the department operates 24 cameras.
notes: Operating; Flock license plate readers announced Sept 2024. Count per police statement to WFMZ as relayed by Lehigh Daily; locations undisclosed and fixed/mobile split not stated. City separately runs non-LPR intersection cameras (not included).

quote: Its three fixed cameras and six mobile cameras have been “transformative for community safety,” saying the system has been used in more than 500 criminal investigations since its installation in 2016.
notes: Operating since 2016 (Motorola Solutions); count is fixed only, 6 vehicle-mounted units excluded. Pennsylvania Capital-Star story syndicated by Tioga Publishing. Department statement (Tri-State Alert, Aug 24, 2026) describes fixed ALPRs at three locations with two more locations to be added, so camera-vs-location count may differ.

quote: The two cameras already operated by Tiverton police are still up and running, Deputy Chief Michael Miguel confirmed to The Herald News.
notes: Operating (2 existing cameras; one was reportedly paid for by a private business owner). Council voted July 27, 2026 to buy 4 more cameras; that order is on hold at the request of the governor and the contract is unsigned. RI State Police separately has 2 Flock cameras in Tiverton (excluded).
